title: CopA3 peptide inhibits MDM2-p53 complex stability in colorectal cancers and activates p53 mediated cell death machinery.
authors: Dey, Debasish Kumar; Sharma, Chanchal; Vadlamudi, Yellamandayya; Kang, Sun Chul
one_liner_zh: 该文研究CopA3肽抑制MDM2-p53蛋白复合物稳定性并激活p53介导的细胞死亡，虽涉及蛋白-蛋白互作与分子对接，但对象为蛋白-蛋白而非蛋白-DNA互作，方法仅含分子对接且无AI/物理模拟深度，与本课题TF-DNA互作关联较弱。
abstract: The diverse expression patterns of the tumor suppressor p53 in cancer cells reflect the regulatory efficiency of multiple cellular pathways. By contrast, many human tumors are reported to develop in the presence of wild-type p53. Recently, several oncogene inhibitors have been used clinically to suppress tumor development by functionally reactivating other oncoproteins. On the other hand, p53 reactivation therapies have not been well established, as few of the p53-MDM2 complex inhibitors such as Nutlin-3 induces mutation in p53 gene upon prolonged usage. Therefore, in this study CopA3, a 9-mer dimeric D-type peptide with anticancer activity against the human colorectal cancer cells, was used to explore the efficacy of p53 reactivation in-vitro and in-vivo. The anticancer activity of CopA3 was more selective towards the wild-type p53 expressing cells than the p53 deficient or mutant colorectal cancer cells. In response to this, this study investigated the signaling pathway in vitro and validated its anti-tumor activity in-vivo. The protein-peptide interaction and molecular docking efficiently provided insight into the specific binding affinity of CopA3 to the p53-binding pocket of the MDM2 protein, which efficiently blocked the p53 and MDM2 interaction. CopA3 plays a crucial role in the binding with MDM2 and enhanced the nuclear translocation of the p53 protein, which sequentially activated the downstream targets to trigger the autophagic mediated cell death machinery through the JNK/Beclin-1 mediated pathway. Collectively, CopA3 affected the MDM2-p53 interaction, which suppressed tumor development. This study may provide a novel inhibitor candidate for the MDM2-p53 complex, which could ultimately suppress the growth of colorectal cancer cells without being cytotoxic to the healthy neighboring cells present around the tumor microenvironment.
abstract_zh: 肿瘤抑制因子p53在癌细胞中的多样化表达模式反映了多条细胞通路的调控效率。相比之下，许多人类肿瘤被报道在野生型p53存在的情况下发展。近年来，几种致癌基因抑制剂已在临床上用于通过功能性再激活其他致癌蛋白来抑制肿瘤发展。另一方面，p53再激活疗法尚未得到充分建立，因为少数p53-MDM2复合物抑制剂如Nutlin-3在长期使用后会诱导p53基因突变。因此，本研究使用CopA3——一种对人大肠癌细胞具有抗癌活性的9聚体二聚D型肽——来探索p53再激活在体外和体内的功效。CopA3的抗癌活性对表达野生型p53的细胞更具选择性，而对p53缺陷或突变的大肠癌细胞选择性较低。针对此，本研究在体外调查了信号通路，并在体内验证了其抗肿瘤活性。蛋白质-肽相互作用和分子对接有效提供了CopA3与MDM2蛋白p53结合口袋特异性结合亲和力的见解，这有效阻断了p53与MDM2的相互作用。CopA3在与MDM2结合中发挥关键作用，并增强了p53蛋白的核转位，随后激活下游靶标，通过JNK/Beclin-1介导的通路触发自噬介导的细胞死亡机制。总体而言，CopA3影响了MDM2-p53相互作用，从而抑制了肿瘤发展。本研究可能为MDM2-p53复合物提供一种新型抑制剂候选物，最终可能在不损害肿瘤微环境周围健康邻近细胞的情况下抑制大肠癌细胞的生长。
